correctness.rationale: Swap symmetry decomposes the exchange-symmetric and exchange-antisymmetric sectors of H=J⊗I+I⊗J+V with D=sum gamma_j |jj><jj|; the antisymmetric sector lies in ker(D) and is H-invariant. If a symmetric H eigenvector has all f_jj=0, the eigen-equation at j=j forces adjacent f_{j,j+1}=0 by induction along the open path. For separation r>=2, the equation at (i,i+r-1) sweeps from the left boundary and forces every f_{i,i+r}=0 because every adjacent hopping is nonzero. Thus the only symmetric dark eigenvector is zero, even for complex hopping and arbitrary exchange-symmetric diagonal V. Finite-dimensional invariant subspaces contain eigenvectors; Hermitian duality gives the entire diagonal detection Krylov span P_+. On K_+ dissipativity forces strictly negative imaginary part for every eigenvalue and Jordan bounds give exponential contraction. Therefore long-time survival is exactly initial P_- weight and for product |u,v> equals (1-|<u,v>|²)/2. Independent randomized Hermitian-path matrices n=2..5 confirmed dark dimensions 1,3,6,10 and long-time survival errors less than 2e-13, strictly corroborative.
